finding.text: The "daily --links backfill adds nothing" check is empty: `Servex/agents/handover.test.mjs:158` only runs `apply_links` when the census already found the child missing, and in that case the assert on line 157 has already failed. So the backfill itself never runs. Call `sr.apply_links(sr.links())` every time, then count the references.

The roll-up test accepts either of two ways to complete the task (`handover.test.mjs:162-163`): if `x: {complete}` is refused, it quietly tries a plain `complete` on the child page. Both runs pass through the first form, so the fallback is dead code that would hide a real refusal. Drop it, or assert which form must work.

With a handoff, `open_task` no longer links the child itself (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:89-92`), and `move_item` writes its `as` reference into the `from` record (`page_tools.js:606`). If `from` is not the child folder's real parent (`parent_task`, or the nearest folder above with a log), that parent gets no reference until the daily `--links` backfill runs. The test only covers the case where `from` is the parent. Linking only when `path.dirname(dir)` differs from `from` would close this gap.

The temp store is a dot-folder inside the real records tree (`handover.test.mjs:123`, `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/22/.handover-test-<pid>`), so the dev server's watchers see it while the test runs. It is removed in `finally`. An `os.tmpdir()` root would be cleaner, if `open_task`/`move_item` accept one.

The brief said to extend an existing process test rather than add a second one. `ProcessRunner.test.mjs` already had a two-step "steps" process (diff lines 50-62), and the new build → review block (lines 64-75) runs a second one beside it. The new block is what checks that a `complete` without evidence is refused, so it earns its place. Putting that refusal check into the existing two-step block would have been simpler.
